comments.body:
I'm trying to narrow down where the working and broken programs are differing, and I think it's in implicit / inferred storage classes, since what's explicitly included in the .spvasm files seems pretty similar. Tint has some code like `DefaultAccessForStorageClass()`, and I imagine there is some analysis of reads and writes that is being ran if we aren't explicit (but I haven't traced through the code to see where that's all happening).

Should we be passing through the `NonWritable` / `NonReadable` decorations?
https://registry.khronos.org/SPIR-V/specs/1.0/SPIRV.html#_a_id_decoration_a_decoration

I could go through and add back the memory access attributes across IREE's dialects, but I first want to pin down how our generated spirv should change (then work backwards from that through the dialects).

+1 to digging in, and those decorations would be nice. We'll need access info anyway for the host side as we need to define the access type on the binding: https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/#enumdef-gpubufferbindingtype needs `read-only-storage` or `storage` and it's used for making implementations aware of data hazards.

Yeah the above error seems to indicate there are deduction logic inside Tint that should be improved. Those `NonWritable`/`NonReadable` is not required for SPIR-V to be valid. Though we can certainly add them using a pass if it helps address the issue; that's not very hard. SPIR-V has this goal of trying to do analysis offline and "attach" the results to avoid driver compilers spending cycles doing that, this actually matches that. (Though driver compilers may not necessary believe in what's coming from the original SPIR-V, so yeah, hard to see the exact effect..)

I see some similar looking issues filed on Tint: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/tint/issues/list?q=storage&can=2

I can try manually adding decorations to the .spvasm that I've been testing with to see if Tint prefers that (thankfully we can hack at IR and dumped files and run passes / tools in isolation - we don't need to jump straight to writing compiler code to test these theories).
Looking quickly at the SPIR-V assembly, this looks like a Tint bug.  The wrong type is being deduced for the pointer for that `let`

This is https://crbug.com/tint/1041
We've let that go dormant.

Ah, nice find, and thanks for looking :)

Can I work around this somehow? I'm fine with making edits to Tint's source for hacking, mostly looking to flush out what else might be blocking us.

One idea was to restore the "memory access" attributes to our interface bindings across flow->stream->hal (see https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/7734). Looking at the sort of IR that triggers this, I'm also skeptical of the `map-memref-spirv-storage-class` pass and how that ends up being used via SPIR-V -> WGSL. Is this unique to codegen, or an issue in flow/stream/hal?

issue.body:
Simple e2e repro, and I'm also adding a lit test hitting this in https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/10134:

```
iree-compile tests/e2e/xla_ops/minimum.mlir -o /dev/null --iree-input-type=mhlo --iree-hal-target-backends=webgpu
...
Tint reported 1 error(s) for a SPIR-V program, see diagnostics:
error: unknown function: 'isNan'
```

The compilation flow looks like roughly:
```mlir
%8 = arith.minf %7, %6 : f32

%6 = arith.cmpf ult, %5, %4 : f32
%7 = arith.select %6, %5, %4 : f32
%8 = arith.cmpf uno, %4, %4 : f32
%9 = arith.select %8, %4, %7 : f32

%8 = spv.FUnordLessThan %7, %5 : f32
%9 = spv.Select %8, %7, %5 : i1, f32
%10 = spv.IsNan %5 : f32
%11 = spv.LogicalOr %10, %10 : i1
%12 = spv.Select %11, %5, %9 : i1, f32
```

WebGPU removed `isInf` and `isNan` back in https://github.com/gpuweb/gpuweb/pull/2311, and Tint removed them in https://dawn.googlesource.com/tint/+/bcd9ad2ebbc183cfbecd75fb6879eb0d55779e5f.

Ideal fixes:

- [ ] Tint could parse `spv.IsNan` (valid SPIR-V) and generate some polyfilled code in WGSL
  - [ ] or WGSL could add back these functions
  - [x] short of those, IREE (spirv dialect?) could add a `CleanUpSPIRVForWGSL` pass that generates such a polyfill
- [x] IREE (arith / spirv dialects?) should generate less `IsNan` and `Select` code - they shouldn't really be needed for many programs unless the user explicitly asks for them

issue.body: Tracking issue for overall [WebGPU](https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/) support in IREE. # Background WebGPU is a recently released API for running graphics and compute workloads on Graphics Processing Units in web browsers. It is similar to modern graphics/compute APIs like Vulkan, D3D12, and Metal, making it a promising target for IREE. At a high level, we need: * IREE's compiler to generate WGSL code * IREE's runtime to have a WebGPU HAL implementation and general web platform support The details can get tricky though: * WGSL is more restrictive than SPIR-V * WebGPU's compute API is more restrictive than Vulkan * Runtime support requires compiling from C to JavaScript/WebAssembly (e.g. via Emscripten and some libraries) # Task breakdown ### Compiler tasks - [x] https://github.com/openxla/iree/issues/7840 - [ ] https://github.com/openxla/iree/issues/10906 - [x] https://github.com/openxla/iree/issues/10908 - [x] https://github.com/openxla/iree/issues/10142 - [x] https://github.com/openxla/iree/issues/10145 - [x] https://github.com/openxla/iree/pull/10224 - [ ] https://github.com/openxla/iree/issues/11054 - [x] https://github.com/openxla/iree/issues/11229 - [ ] https://github.com/openxla/iree/issues/11321 - [ ] https://github.com/openxla/iree/issues/12509 - [x] https://github.com/openxla/iree/pull/13965 ### Runtime tasks - [x] https://github.com/openxla/iree/pull/13952 - [x] https://github.com/openxla/iree/pull/13669 - [ ] https://github.com/openxla/iree/issues/13809 - [x] https://github.com/openxla/iree/pull/13962 - [ ] Web Workers for threading (optional) - [ ] Implement semaphores and use for asynchronous queue execution callbacks ### Infrastructure / developer experience tasks - [x] WebGPU/WGSL compiler builds and tests running on presubmit - [x] General Wasm/Emscripten runtime build running on postsubmit - [ ] WebGPU runtime build running on postsubmit - [ ] All web builds running on presubmit (move out of `experimental/`) - [ ] Write async unit tests, runnable in some way - [ ] Integrate tests into CI - [ ] Document how to use Wasm/WebGPU builds ### Other related issues - [ ] https://github.com/openxla/iree/issues/6499 - [ ] https://github.com/openxla/iree/issues/8327 # # Status _last updated 2023-08-03_ * All code is merged onto the `main` branch * The application at [`experimental/web/sample_webgpu`](https://github.com/iree-org/iree/tree/main/experimental/web/sample_webgpu) can programs in web browsers without crashing but with incorrect results * multiple_results.mlir: `absf(-1.23, -4.56)` returns `(4.56, 0)` at first, then `(1.23, 4.56)` on future calls with the same loaded program state * mobilebert, posenet, mobilessd: no errors, correct number of outputs, incorrect numerical results (way off llvm-cpu/local-task, stable across runs) * A few compiler options are still needed to work around codegen feature gaps ## Previous status reports: ### 2023-05-26 * The [`webgpu` branch](https://github.com/iree-org/iree/tree/webgpu) hosting the runtime HAL and a sample webpage (.c, .js, Emscripten) is close to `main` * https://github.com/openxla/iree/pull/13815 gets it ready for merging into `experimental/` * The application at [`experimental/web/sample_webgpu`](https://github.com/iree-org/iree/tree/webgpu/experimental/web/sample_webgpu) can run `simple_abs`, `fullyconnected`, and MobileSSD using WebGPU in web browsers * tested Chrome 113 on Windows and Chrome Dev on Linux with Vulkan launch flags * Posenet, MobileBERT, and other programs with more than one output hit https://github.com/openxla/iree/issues/13809 * https://github.com/openxla/iree/pull/13820 will async-ify `experimental/web/sample_webgpu/` using `iree_loop_emscripten` * A few compiler options are required as workarounds, depending on the input program. Currently these are `--iree-codegen-gpu-native-math-precision=true` and `alias-mutable-bindings` (no tool flag, edit in source) ### 2022-12-14 [IREE WebGPU Status 2022-12-14](https://gist.github.com/ScottTodd/a5090171b8b6b9b089a7515943e0b611) ### 2022-10-04 [IREE WebGPU Status 2022-10-04](https://gist.github.com/ScottTodd/63450504acce513d3fef3b8c018234e2)
